svg.font-family: Iowan Old Style, Palatino, Georgia, serif
svg.title: All-to-all vs. all-reduce as communication patterns
svg.desc: All-reduce: every GPU contributes a partial tensor and every GPU ends with the identical summed result — one shared answer. All-to-all: every GPU sends a different personalized shard to every other GPU and receives a different shard back from each — a full regrouping, not a reduction. All-to-all is harder to schedule because its payload is data-dependent (skewed by routing) rather than fixed-size like an all-reduce.
svg.text: All-reduce (one answer) vs. all-to-all (a full regroup)
every GPU ends holding the SAME sum
each GPU sends a DIFFERENT shard to each other
payload size is data-dependent — hard to schedule
A reduction has one fixed-size answer; a regroup's shape depends on where tokens routed — that's the scheduling problem.
